teaser.text: HCA Healthcare runs hospitals and related sites where people receive medical care. It sells access to the clinicians, rooms, equipment and treatment that turn a serious symptom into diagnosis, care and recovery, then collects from insurers, government programs and patients.

stock.title: HCA stock forecast
stock.meta_description: HCA stock forecast: weighted scenarios, cash generation, risks and valuation through October 2029.
stock.opening: HCA's weighted forecast is $469.67 in October 2027, $513.34 in October 2028 and $564.83 in October 2029; the base case receives 50% probability, the bear case 30%, and the bull case 20%. It hinges on whether coverage losses stabilize and cash generation funds capital spending and repurchases without materially higher debt.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how HCA runs its business, compares with rivals, assesses management and weighs risks.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for HCA?

paragraphs.text: The bear case keeps margins below the recent 9.0% level as uninsured care and payment pressure persist. Earnings fall from $5,966 million to $5,960 million across the forecast dates. The bull case reaches $8,372 million as volume, productivity and new capacity lift margins to 9.2%. The reduced 2026 outlook anchors the forecast, while the $423 million Florida catch-up contribution is excluded because it relates to earlier care.

blocks.heading: How much cash does HCA really make?

paragraphs.text: Capital spending then consumed $4,944 million, leaving $7,692 million of common free cash flow. Stock compensation added back $401 million in accounting cash flow but gave employees an ownership claim; deducting it produces analytical “real free cash flow” of $7,291 million. Working capital also released $418 million in 2025, after tying up $106 million in 2024. That favorable timing may not repeat.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for HCA today?

paragraphs.text: At $469.91, HCA trades at 15.7 times trailing earnings. P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, tells investors how many dollars they pay for each dollar of annual profit per share. Its 14.6 times forward P/E implies about $32.19 of earnings per share over the next twelve months, above the revised 2026 guidance of $28.70 to $30.50. Because that forward period reaches into 2027, the price assumes earnings recover beyond the weaker current-year outlook.

dividend.opening: HCA pays $0.78 per share each quarter, and its base case raises dividends from $3.30 to $3.78 per share. In 2025, $7,692 million of free cash flow covered $679 million of dividends, although total shareholder payouts exceeded free cash flow.
dividend.closing: The full memo also examines HCA’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does HCA pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise modestly in the base case, from $3.30 to $3.54 and then $3.78 per share. The latest quarterly rate is $0.78, while free cash flow was $7,692 million in 2025, supporting increases. The bear case holds the dividend at $3.12 before a small recovery; the bull case reaches $4.08. Recent dividend growth supports the base, but the 2020 suspension shows that severe pressure can interrupt it.

blocks.heading: Does HCA’s dividend come from free cash flow?

paragraphs.subsection: 5.9 — Can HCA fund its capital needs and debt while returning cash?
paragraphs.text: Free cash flow was $7,692 million, while repurchases cost $10,067 million and dividends cost $679 million. Distributions therefore exceeded free cash flow by roughly $3,054 million before acquisitions and minority distributions. Debt increased and cash fell, so the gap was a financing choice rather than a cash surplus.

blocks.heading: What has HCA guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Diluted EPS guidance is $28.70–$30.50. HCA expects $5.0–$5.5 billion of capital expenditures. The guidance includes a $1.0–$1.2 billion exchange headwind. It also includes $300–$500 million from Medicaid supplemental-payment programs.

blocks.heading: Did HCA keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management also exceeded its original 2025 forecasts for adjusted EBITDA and diluted earnings per share. Guidance is an estimate, not a guarantee, and outside events can help, but the result supports the financial case for the rewards.

blocks.heading: What has HCA's revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: Q2 2026 showed more activity but weaker underlying economics. Revenue rose 8.7% to $20,230 million, while operating income rose only 3.7% and operating margin fell to approximately 15.3%. EPS rose 11.6% to $7.62, again helped by fewer shares rather than equivalent growth in total profit.

HCA also estimated that uninsured patients reduced pretax income by approximately $400 million. Cash flow weakened sharply: operating cash flow fell to $2,335 million and free cash flow to $1,104 million. Same-facility admissions rose 2.5%, but inpatient surgeries fell 2.3%, outpatient surgeries fell 3.4% and emergency visits rose 3.6%. More care, therefore, did not mean better care economics.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in HCA's next results?

paragraphs.text: HCA’s next scheduled earnings call is October 27, 2026. The important combination is uninsured admissions, surgery volumes and collections. More admissions support demand, but demand helps less when fewer patients have coverage. Management also expects fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA growth to exceed third-quarter growth, making year-end results a test of its revised assumptions.
